CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to his current treatment regimen. While he has adhered to the prescribed sertraline at 200 mg daily and has successfully reduced his lorazepam use to once a week, he continues to experience significant challenges with sleep. He reports an average of 5 hours of sleep per night, with persistent difficulty initiating sleep and frequent awakenings. The patient has noted that the trazodone, which was initiated at the last visit at a dose of 50 mg nightly, has provided some improvement in sleep quality, allowing him to feel slightly more rested upon awakening.
Despite this improvement, Mr. Smith describes ongoing fatigue, particularly in the afternoons, which he attributes to both his disrupted sleep and increased workload. He has documented an increase in headache frequency, now occurring four times weekly, with intensity rated as 7/10 during episodes. He continues to take amitriptyline at 20 mg nightly and ibuprofen as needed, but reports that the headaches have become more resistant to over-the-counter analgesics. Mr. Smith has also increased the frequency of his acupuncture sessions to twice a week, expressing hope that this will yield further relief.
He remains committed to his yoga practice and mindfulness techniques, yet acknowledges that work-related stressors continue to impact his overall well-being.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (new medication) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 6. Amitriptyline 20 mg nightly 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage decreased)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that project deadlines remain a source of stress. He has maintained his commitment to physical activity, attending yoga classes regularly and incorporating meditation practices into his routine. He abstains from alcohol and adheres to a plant-based diet, although he occasionally indulges in processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Persistent difficulty initiating sleep; anxiety manageable but worsens at night; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Increased headache frequency and intensity; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Notable fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce the tapering of lorazepam use. Monitor for any signs of withdrawal or increased anxiety. Schedule a follow-up with a therapist for cognitive-behavioral therapy to enhance coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg; evaluate the need for a potential increase in dosage if sleep quality does not improve. Continue melatonin at 10 mg; maintain CBT-I strategies and closely monitor sleep patterns. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Due to increased frequency and intensity, consider increasing amitriptyline to 30 mg nightly. Assess the impact of acupuncture and discuss the potential for preventive medication such as topiramate if headaches persist despite these adjustments. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Emphasize the importance of maintaining physical activity and mindfulness practices. Consider a referral to a nutritionist for dietary optimization. Explore sleep hygiene techniques to further improve sleep quality.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-12-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
